title: The Unsolved Murder of Hall and Mills
summary: Chuck and Josh (with a guest-style co-host segment) cover the 1922 Hall-Mills murders in New Brunswick, New Jersey: Episcopal reverend Edward Hall and his parishioner/mistress Eleanor Mills were found shot and mutilated under a crab apple tree on a path off Lover's Lane near the Phillips farm in Somerset County. The episode covers the staged crime scene, jurisdictional fights, the crowds that stripped the scene, the wrongful focus on Ray Schneider, Pearl Bamber, and Clifford Hayes, the suspicion falling on Francis Hall and her brothers and cousin, the pig farmer Jane Gibson's testimony, the 1926 reopening after a divorce case, the love letters, the 1926 trial and acquittal, and later theories including the Klan and The Great Gatsby connection. The episode closes with listener mail about cigarette prices in Australia.
topics: William Kunstler Minister in the Choir Singer
Stuff You Should Know true crime

segments.title: Opening banter and People magazine question
segments.summary: Hosts open the show, discuss the episode's true-crime tone, and joke about where the idea came from, including a People magazine article and the Great Gatsby connection.

segments.title: Victims and background
segments.summary: Edward Hall, an Episcopal pastor at St. John's in New Brunswick, and his mistress Eleanor Mills, a choir member and his assistant, are introduced. Francis Hall's wealthy family and the couple's open-secret affair are described, along with Hall's motives regarding her money.

segments.title: Discovery of the bodies and staged scene
segments.summary: The affair is an open secret; the lovers exchanged notes. The bodies were found on a path off Lover's Lane near the Phillips farm, shot execution-style and mutilated, posed under a crab apple tree, with love letters and a business card placed around them.
topics: Pearl Bamber and Ray Schneider discovery

segments.title: Crowds and compromised crime scene
segments.summary: Thousands of curious onlookers came, took souvenirs and dirt, and trampled the scene while two counties disputed jurisdiction. Blood evidence in the soil was lost.
topics: jurisdiction dispute Middlesex and Somerset counties

segments.title: Suspects, theories, and false arrest
segments.summary: Robbery and Klan theories are considered; Italian men are briefly mentioned. Ray Schneider, Pearl Bamber, Clifford Hayes, and Leon Kaufman are questioned for about 24 hours, Schneider signs a false confession, Hayes is arrested, and Schneider and Bamber are later sentenced for false statements.

segments.title: Police handling and public reaction
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the flawed police work and the press and public skepticism toward the arrest of Hayes.

segments.title: Suspicion on Francis Hall and family, Jane Gibson's sighting
segments.summary: Police eventually questioned Francis Hall, whose story shifted; her brother Willie lacked a solid alibi, and brother Henry claimed a fishing alibi. Jane Gibson, the pig farmer nicknamed the pig woman, said she saw the family members commit the murders.

segments.title: 1922 grand jury, 1926 reopening, and new evidence
segments.summary: A 1922 grand jury declined to indict. Francis Hall went to Italy. In 1926, a divorce case involving former maid Louise Geist's husband revived the case and Governor Harry Moore ordered it reopened. Witnesses including Ralph Gorsline and Paul Amborski came forward, and the love letters were read in court.

segments.title: 1926 trial, acquittal, and later theories
segments.summary: The 1926 trial lasted 23 days. Jane Gibson testified on a stretcher, Francis Hall was called the iron widow, and Willie's testimony helped secure the acquittal in December 1926. The defendants sued the Mirror for libel and settled. William Kunstler's 1964 book suggested the Klan; the Great Gatsby link is discussed.

segments.title: Class themes and sources
segments.summary: Hosts compare the neglect of Eleanor Mills's working-class death with the wealthy family's story and thank sources.

segments.title: Listener mail: cigarette prices in Australia
segments.summary: A listener from Melbourne writes about the high price of cigarettes in Australia and compares it to the cost of coffee and holidays.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give the podcast's distribution information.
